verdict.rationale: WorkOS documents AuthKit as a spec-compatible OAuth authorization server that can be placed in front of an MCP server to manage access, with built-in MCP and OAuth application support. Token verification is only indirectly evidenced through session JWTs and SDK JWKS helpers, and there is no documented evidence of per-scope token issuance for remote MCP agents. missing for 10: explicit documentation of scoped access tokens for MCP clients, details of the MCP-specific spec features (e.g. discovery and dynamic client registration), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can put a spec-compliant OAuth authorization flow in front of my MCP server so remote agents connect with scoped, verifiable tokens

citations.quote: WorkOS and AuthKit can provide a secure way to manage access to your MCP server with minimal effort.
AuthKit, which is a spec-compatible OAuth authorization server.
Built-in support for MCP and OAuth applications.
